prompt: You are the test author this time: write isCorrect so it accepts a correct LengthSorter and rejects broken ones. Complete the checker in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: A tie-break is only tested by a tie: every one of these implementations agrees about a list whose words all have different lengths, so an input like ["pear", "fig", "kiwi", "date"] -- where two words are four letters long -- is doing all the work. The in-place bug needs the same trick as any "returns a new collection" contract: hold your own reference to the input, and check afterwards that its order is unchanged. Note that the input has to be a mutable list for that check to mean anything, since sorting an immutable List.of would throw rather than quietly succeed.
hints: Your input needs at least two words of the SAME length, or the alphabetical tie-break is never exercised. ["pear", "fig", "kiwi", "date"] works.
Build the input with new ArrayList<>(...) and check its order again after the call -- one implementation sorts the list you handed it.
Add an all-same-length list such as ["cow", "ant", "bee"]: it isolates the alphabetical rule from the length rule.
